issues: Vulnerable dependencies remain in the Expo app: braces 3.0.3 (CVE-2026-93687) and node-forge 1.4.0 (CVE-2026-85393) are still present in package-lock.json and are detected by Trivy. The postinstall scripts (deleteVulnDeps.cjs and deleteNodeForge.cjs) do not reliably remove these transitive dependencies because they only delete top‑level entries and miss nested packages, leaving the vulnerabilities unfixed. Update the project dependencies to versions without these vulnerabilities (or ensure the scripts correctly remove all occurrences of braces and node-forge from the lockfile and that the vulnerable packages are not installed).

The security scan still reports a medium‑severity uuid 7.0.3 vulnerability. Although package.json specifies uuid "^13.0.0", an old uuid version is still present in the lockfile as a transitive dependency. Ensure the lockfile is updated so that only safe uuid versions are installed, or apply an appropriate resolution/override to eliminate the vulnerable version.

While the /media endpoint now checks authentication and ownership, it still directly serves files from the file system using FileResponse. Consider adding proper content‑type headers and further hardening, or replace the endpoint with signed URLs from a secure storage backend to fully mitigate file‑serving risks.
feedback: The authentication and most security hardening (rate limiting, security headers, upload validation) are correctly implemented, but the vulnerable dependency removal is incomplete, leaving known security issues in the client bundle. Fix the dependency issues as described, and optionally improve the media serving approach to meet the full security requirements.
